The current first-party careers handoff identifies the employer-bound public native client. Normal anonymous All Jobs filteredjobs POST (pageType=0, all filters null) returns Total7 and seven unique IDs; every full public DTO is fetched with the normal fieldVisibility=CareerPage query and matched to its public JobPosting and closing snapshot before caller caps. The old advertised careerpage has a misleading vacancy-free view. Explicit native job work countries establish India. All source CAREERPAGE dates remain August 6; no source expiry is advertised. Source dates, general publication, native experience, skills, zero requisition GUID as null, and actual application template IDs remain distinct. Current client/CSS hashes and visual/executable inventories reject unreviewed changes. No login, application action, candidate/private API, database or pipeline invocation. The current declared TurboHire bootstrap and public route clients are supported with exact byte hashes. Corporate publisher, native employer, country, full description and closing role context still require validation. A current zero board or a complete declared board cannot certify company-wide inventory or enable lifecycle cleanup.

Two full global native All Jobs snapshots and every public role DTO/JobPosting are reconciled with corporate proxy IDs, full criteria, explicit work country, CAREERPAGE publication and expiry, native application context and employer binding before caller caps. FilteredJobs Total must equal the unique returned set; unreviewed continuation metadata or corporate/native gaps retain partial status. Remote placeholders require an explicit role-owned India Location label and matching native country schema. General/CAREERPAGE dates remain distinct; source midnight expiry without timezone retains day precision. Zero requisition GUIDs remain null and JobCode stays separate. Anonymous public reader credentials remain only in memory. Only the reviewed public listing POSTs are used; no login, candidate/application action, private API, database or pipeline invocation. The current declared TurboHire bootstrap and public route clients are supported with exact byte hashes.
